Transcription regulators and ultra-rare and other rare translocation-related sarcomas treated with trabectedin: A proof of principle from a post-hoc analysis. Front Oncol 2022;12:1042479. PMID 36568164 · PMC9780071 · doi 10.3389/fonc.2022.1042479.
what_it_supports: ⭐ THE SECOND EMC-SPECIFIC TRABECTEDIN RESPONSE DENOMINATOR THAT EXISTS, and the only one carrying an EMC patient with progressive disease on the drug. A post-hoc case series of the ultra-rare and other rare translocation-related sarcoma patients inside TrObs, the Italian Sarcoma Group's non-interventional retrospective study of trabectedin in routine practice (NCT02793050; 512 anthracycline-pretreated patients, 20 Italian sites, enrolled 2010-2015). Of the 36 patients, three had EMC, and Table 2's EMC row reads 0 objective responses, 2 stable disease, 1 progressive disease — disease control 2 of 3. ⛔ IT IS NOT A BETTER CASE FOR THE DRUG: it enlarges the EMC denominator on which the objective-response count for trabectedin is still ZERO. ⚠ SCOPE, FOUR PARTS. (1) NO EMC-SPECIFIC PFS OR OS IS REPORTED — Table 3 breaks PFS out by histology only for the three histologies that produced a response, and EMC is not among them; that is an absence in the paper, not an absence of the reading. (2) Response was assessed by the TREATING PHYSICIAN per RECIST 1.1, not by central radiology review, which is the opposite of EV-MORIOKA's basis. (3) Retrospective and non-interventional. (4) ⛔ POPULATION OVERLAP WITH chiusole2020's 'second line ... trabectedin 66% of 3' IS UNRESOLVED and this record is therefore CONTEXT rather than pooled evidence — same n, same 2-of-3 disease control, an overlapping enrolment window, and one author in common at Istituto Oncologico Veneto. No efficacy, safety, eligibility or clinical-readiness claim is made for EMC.

what_it_supports: The CASSINI trial (ambulatory cancer, Khorana score ≥2, rivaroxaban vs placebo, n=841 randomized): the primary composite endpoint (proximal DVT, PE, symptomatic distal/upper-limb DVT, OR DEATH FROM VENOUS THROMBOEMBOLISM) did NOT differ significantly over the full 180-day trial period -- 6.0% vs 8.8%, HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.40-1.09, p=0.10. It DID differ during the on-treatment intervention period only (2.6% vs 6.4%, HR 0.40). The trial's own conclusion, quoted: 'treatment with rivaroxaban did not result in a significantly lower incidence of venous thromboembolism or death due to venous thromboembolism in the 180-day trial period.' This is the closest primary-source statement to an event-rate-vs-death distinction available from the abstract; it is a VTE-related-death composite, not an all-cause overall-survival analysis.

citation: Temel JS, Greer JA, Muzikansky A, Gallagher ER, Admane S, Jackson VA, Dahlin CM, Blinderman CD, Jacobsen J, Pirl WF, Billings JA, Lynch TJ. Early palliative care for patients with metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer. N Engl J Med 2010;363(8):733-742. PMID 20818875 · doi 10.1056/nejmoa1000678.
what_it_supports: THE FOUNDING TRIAL of RT-EARLY-PALLIATIVE's premise. Newly diagnosed metastatic NSCLC (n=151), randomized to early palliative care integrated with standard oncologic care vs standard care alone. Despite less aggressive end-of-life care in the intervention arm (33% vs 54%, p=0.05), median OVERALL SURVIVAL was LONGER with early palliative care: 11.6 vs 8.9 months, p=0.02. Also improved quality of life (FACT-L 98.0 vs 91.5, p=0.03) and fewer depressive symptoms (16% vs 38%, p=0.01). Population is metastatic NSCLC, median survival on the order of months -- a far shorter natural history than EMC's; any application to EMC is a TRANSFER, not a direct finding.

PMID 38558247 · PMC11449095 · doi 10.1093/oncolo/oyae050.
what_it_supports: AN INDEPENDENT REPLICATION of EV-TEMEL-2010's survival finding, in a different (Mexican/LMIC) setting -- the transfer question RT-EARLY-PALLIATIVE's rationale asks about most directly answered for a second, geographically distinct population. Advanced NSCLC (n=146), EPC vs standard oncologic care (SOC), primary endpoint overall survival. Median OS 18.1 months (EPC) vs 10.5 months (SOC), HR 1.5 [95% CI 1.04-2.3], p=.030 -- longer survival with EPC. The benefit concentrated in patients with good baseline performance status/quality of life (post hoc subgroup: ECOG 0-1, HR 1.6 [1.03-2.5], p=.037; GQoL>70, p=.048); no significant difference in the poor-performance-status/low-QoL subgroup. Still NSCLC, still a months-scale survival population -- the transfer to EMC's decade-scale natural history is unaddressed by this trial and remains open.

citation: Kochovska S, Ferreira DH, Luckett T, Phillips JL, Currow DC. Earlier multidisciplinary palliative care intervention for people with lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Transl Lung Cancer Res 2020;9(6):2721-2735. PMID 32953543 · PMC7481603 · doi 10.21037/tlcr.2019.12.18.
what_it_supports: The evidence-base context as of 2020, BEFORE the PACO and Chongqing replications existed: at that point survival data for early palliative care came from only TWO studies, one lung-cancer-specific (EV-TEMEL-2010) and one in a mixed advanced-cancer population comparing EARLY (30-60 days) vs DELAYED (3 months) palliative care referral -- not early-vs-none -- which found longer 1-year survival with earlier referral (63% vs 48%, difference 15%, p=0.038). ⚠ THIS IS A DIFFERENT COMPARISON THAN TEMEL'S (timing-within-palliative-care, not presence-vs-absence) and must not be conflated with it. Quality-of-life and symptom outcomes were mixed/non-significant across most of the other studies reviewed. Establishes that, as of 2020, the survival claim rested on a thin base (2 studies) -- the two subsequent RCTs (EV-PACO-2024, EV-CHEN-2023-CEPC) materially strengthen it.
